notes: First correct fp32 no-transpose M-block-outer streaming GEMM (out=lhs^T@rhs, M4096 K2048 N10944). NO explicit transpose stage: the reshape (K,.)->(128,16,.) maps k=k_in*16+kt so K is on the PARTITION axis of both v1/v2, and nc_matmul(stationary,moving)=stationary.T@moving computes lhs^T@rhs directly (transposed-lhs operand is a free byproduct of the input layout; same idiom the NKIBench baseline uses). M-block-outer: 4 blocks of 1024 rows, lhs_blk [128,16,1024] resident/block, rhs streamed in N_CHUNK=456 chunks reused across 8 subtiles => rhs re-read 4x not 32x. N_CHUNK=456 exact divisor of 10944 (456*24) and <=512 fp32 PSUM width => ZERO tail masking anywhere (baseline uses N_CHUNK=1024 with mask=...>=0; deliberately removed). fp32 end-to-end, zero-init PSUM accumulator, 16-tile kt PSUM accumulation, single copy+store per output tile. FULL 5-seed PASS: per-seed rel-L2=3.99e-7 UNIFORM (all seeds, ~50x under the 2e-5 gate); verify.py PASS (gates l2_norm_passed). PE-BOUND at fp32 floor: PE=99.8% MFU=49% TRUE-PE-active 4.718ms~=p50; Vec5% Scl0% DMA21% (hidden). HBMrd=392MB EXACT (lhs 33.5 x1 + rhs 89.6 x4) HBMwr=179MB EXACT (out x1), no spill (psum_read 768 = one drain/tile). matmul_instruction_count 24576 = 2.0 instr/site (fp32 emulates in 2 passes). 1.026x over 4.849615ms baseline. KEPT as the guaranteed pure-fp32 fallback. See profile/tmm_v1_digest.md.

OFFLINE GATE (runs/offline_bf16_split_sim.py, pure GEMM): fp32 control 0.000e+00, worst 3-product 4.453e-6 << 2e-5. ON-DEVICE full-5-seed PASS: rel-L2=4.4515e-6 UNIFORM, l2_norm_passed=True; quadrature back-out 4.4336e-6 == offline within 0.41%. SPEED: --fast p50 3.8713ms, full-5-seed 3.8699ms, RAW tensor_engine_active_time_ns 9431025->7262192 = -23.0% (window-independent). matmul_instruction_count 24576->36864 (2.0->3.0/site); per-instr fp32 rate 0.192us vs bf16 0.098us = fp32 1.95x. NO SPILL (hbm_write 179.3MB + psum_read 768 byte-identical) BUT hbm_read 392->448MB (+14.2%): compiler re-fetches ~15% of rhs tiles under the larger bf16-limb working set at M_BLK=8. This VIOLATES AC-4 (read must stay near the 392MB floor), so v2 is ARCHIVED, not promoted -- the branch that motivated the M_BLK fix. Fused-lo variant tmm_v2b_bf16_split_tight is byte-identical (residual buffer not the cause). See profile/tmm_v2_bf16_split_digest.md.

PROMOTED (first transpose_matmul kernel to beat v1's 1.026x). Same compensated bf16x2 3-product split as tmm_v2 (numerically identical: rel-L2 4.4515e-6 uniform on full-5-seed, l2_norm_passed=True), but M_BLK=16 (2 blocks of 2048 rows) instead of M_BLK=8 (4 blocks). This HALVES the rhs read multiple (rhs re-streamed once per M-block: x2 not x4), fixing v2's AC-4 read regression: FULL-RUN hbm_read=229.0MB (-41.6% vs v1's 392MB floor, well below), hbm_write 179.3MB + psum_read_sbuf_write_count 768 BYTE-IDENTICAL (NO SPILL). Low limb produced directly by residual subtract into a bf16 destination (no separate fp32 residual buffer). Full-5-seed p50 3.6338ms; RAW tensor_engine_active_time_ns 9431025->7126656 = -24.4% vs v1 (window-independent, v1 anchors agree 0.002%). PE 98%, MFU 48%. matmul_instruction_count 36864 (3.0/site). D3/M_BLK lever ADOPTED (gated in: D1 shifted DMA off hidden + AC-4 needed a fix; it WON, not the flagged anti-lever, because it cuts the rhs read multiple; 128KB/part resident limbs still fit, peak ~168KB<192KB). THIRD (cleanest) WIN at 2.0-instr/site after matmul_add_rmsnorm (pure GEMM, mechanism isolated). tmm_v1 kept as fp32 fallback. See profile/tmm_v2_bf16_split_digest.md.

MEASURED REJECT (N_CHUNK=512 wider-chunk screen composed on tmm_v3_mblk16). N tiled as 21 full 512-wide chunks + one 192-wide tail (22 chunk-groups vs 24 at N_CHUNK=456); tail is a SEPARATE narrow chunk (no mask arithmetic, correct-by-construction). Correct: rel-L2 4.4515e-6, l2_norm_passed=True. matmul_instruction_count 36864->33792 (-8.3%), psum_read_sbuf_write_count 768->704. BUT same-session bracket v3a->v4->v3b: v3 band 0.0055%, v4 p50 3.6762ms REGRESSES +1.12% vs v3 3.6353ms (>> band); TRUE PE-active RISES 3.564->3.575ms; hbm_read 229->257MB. The -8% instruction saving does NOT convert to PE-active -- the kernel is PE-COLUMN-bound not issue-overhead-bound, and the 192-wide tail under-fills. Exactly the AC-7 negative test (adopting D2 on an instruction-count improvement alone without a wall win). D2 rejected; tmm_v3_mblk16 stays promoted. See profile/tmm_v2_bf16_split_digest.md.

MEASURED REJECT (the plan-exact N_CHUNK=512 + MASKED-tail D2 screen, composed on tmm_v3_mblk16). N=10944 tiled as 22 uniform 512-wide chunks (ceil(10944/512)); the last chunk's 320 out-of-range columns masked via valid_n = (N-1)-(512*c+inc) >= 0 on the rhs LOAD (invalid lanes load zero -> zero limbs -> zero matmul contribution) and the output STORE (no out-of-range write). Mirrors the NKIBench baseline mask idiom. CORRECT: rel-L2 4.4515e-6, l2_norm_passed=True, hbm_write 179306496 EXACT (mask boundary works, no OOB write). matmul_instruction_count 36864->33792 (-8.3%), psum_read_sbuf_write_count 768->704. BUT same-session bracket v3a->v5->v3b: v3 band 0.0138%, v5 p50 3.7887ms REGRESSES +4.2% vs v3 3.6362ms (>> band); TRUE PE-active 3.564->3.678ms (+3.2%); hbm_read 229->253MB. This is WORSE than the mask-free separate-tail v4 (+1.12%): the tail-mask arithmetic on load+store adds overhead ON TOP OF the wider-chunk non-benefit. Confirms the AC-7 negative test (instruction-count win without a wall win) AND the plan's own warning that reintroducing the mask arithmetic (phase-1 removed it) is a cost. D2 rejected in BOTH forms (mask-free v4 +1.12%, masked v5 +4.2%); tmm_v3_mblk16 stays promoted at 1.334x. See profile/tmm_phase2r2_*.txt.

MEASURED REJECT (E1 gap-only screen: widen the rhs-limb BUILD chunk 456->912 to halve the prologue count, composed on tmm_v3_mblk16). CLEAN ISOLATION: limbs built over a 912-wide chunk (12 prologues/block vs 24) but matmul moving width kept at 456 (two 456-wide sub-chunks per 912 build) -> matmul_instruction_count 36864 BYTE-IDENTICAL to v3, same PSUM/PE columns; the ONLY changed variable is the rhs-limb build granularity (NOT the chunk-WIDTH change v4/v5 already rejected). Correct: rel-L2 4.4515e-6, l2_norm_passed=True. BUT same-session bracket v3a->v6->v3b (--fast): v3 band |v3a-v3b| = 0.03% wall / 0.08% PE-active; v6 p50 7.3303ms REGRESSES +101.6% vs v3 3.6355ms (>> band), TRUE PE-active/inf RISES 3.5630->4.0458ms (+13.5%), hbm_read 229->1765MB (7.7x, AC-4 FAIL), hbm_write 179.3->259.6MB (+45% = SPILL, AC-4 FAIL). Mechanism: 912-wide rhs limbs 2x[128,16,912] bf16 ~= 57KB/part (vs 28.5 at 456) on top of 128KB/part resident lhs limbs + transient fp32 build tiles pushes peak SBUF over the ~192KB budget -> compiler spills bf16 limbs and re-fetches. Enlarged-resident-live-set anti-lever (bmm cross-batch class) measured directly on this op. The halved prologue count never mattered: v3's limb build is ALREADY fully hidden (Vec 13.7%/Scl 6.7%/GpSimd 14.2%/DMA 22.5% all << PE 98%). E1 rejected; tmm_v3_mblk16 stays promoted at 1.334x. See profile/tmm_phase3_v6_nchunk912.txt, tmm_phase3_v3a.txt, tmm_phase3_v3b.txt.

MEASURED REJECT (E2 double-buffer/PREFETCH rhs limbs; FAITHFUL build-ahead schedule, reworked in R2 per Codex R1 review from the R1 build-both-then-matmul batch). Two FIXED resident rhs-limb sets A/B per M-block; prime A<-chunk0, then for p=0..10 build B<-2p+1 (prefetch), matmul A(2p), build A<-2p+2 (prefetch), matmul B(2p+1); final pair build B<-23, matmul A(22), matmul B(23). Straight-line Python-unroll (NOT sequential_range) so each build-ahead overlaps the preceding chunk matmul. M_BLK=16, N_CHUNK=456, 3 products, layout unchanged -> matmul_instruction_count 36864 BYTE-IDENTICAL, rel-L2 4.4515e-6 (correct, pure reschedule). Same-session bracket v3a->v7->v3b: v3 band 0.011% wall (3.6356/3.6352); v7 p50 3.6256ms is 0.27% FASTER (TRUE PE-active 3.5567ms, -0.2% vs v3 -- the prefetch DID overlap a sliver of limb-build) BUT the gain is << the 3% adopt bar and inside the ~2% PE-idle ceiling. REJECTED on AC-4: hbm_read 229->283.4MB (+23.8%) AND hbm_write 179.3->183.0MB (+2.1% small write-spill) -- both fixed limb sets live the whole N-sweep enlarge the working set, inducing rhs re-fetch + a little spill (larger read than the R1 batch v7 257MB because both sets are live longer). Exactly the tmm_v2 M_BLK=8 case: faster-but-read-floor-breaking is rejected on the immutable AC-4, a real wall win cannot waive it. The double-buffer mechanism WORKS (prefetch engaged) but is not worth its memory cost. tmm_v3_mblk16 stays promoted at 1.334x. See profile/tmm_phase3r2_v7_dbuf.txt, tmm_phase3r2_v3a.txt, tmm_phase3r2_v3b.txt.
